name: ASUS router (AiMesh)
author: Netlens
description: Reads which device is connected to which AiMesh node (stock ASUSWRT, tested on an RT-AX92U) for the hierarchy and the map, the router's Traffic Analyzer (traffic per application and per device), and the health of the router and every node: processor, memory, temperature, uptime, firmware, ports and interface speeds (internet, LAN, Wi-Fi). Read-only, never SSH: one login per router, a few reads and a logout per sync. A refused login pauses automatic syncing.

config.label: Router address
config.help: The router's web interface. HTTPS defaults to port 8443.

config.label: Verify TLS certificate
config.help: Leave off: ASUS routers use a self-signed certificate.

config.label: Read the Traffic Analyzer statistics
config.help: Needs Traffic Analyzer switched on in the router (Adaptive QoS > Traffic Analyzer > Statistic). The first figures appear about an hour after switching it on.

config.label: Record the health of the routers
config.help: Processor, memory, temperature and uptime, the physical ports, and the speed of the internet connection (WAN), the wired LAN and the Wi-Fi radios. A few extra reads per router per sync; nothing to switch on in the router.

config.label: Read the AiMesh nodes too
config.help: The nodes accept the main router's user name and password. Netlens asks each node at the address the router lists for it on every sync, so a node that gets another address is still found; nothing to set up per node. A node that refuses the login is skipped.
